findings.explanation: The SearchResultSerializer is moved from src/documents/views.py (where it inherited from PassUserMixin) to src/documents/serialisers.py (where it only inherits from DocumentSerializer). PassUserMixin's get_serializer method passes the current user to the serializer context, which is critical for authorization checks on object-level permissions. The policy states that documents have object-level permissions with owners and permission sets that must be enforced. By removing PassUserMixin inheritance, the serializer no longer receives the user context in get_serializer(), breaking the authorization flow. The to_representation method fetches documents by ID without any user permission verification (line 809 in PR: Document.objects.get(id=instance["id"])), and without the user context passed by PassUserMixin, downstream serialization via DocumentSerializer's parent OwnedObjectSerializer/SerializerWithPerms cannot enforce object-level access controls.

evidence.content: All objects (documents, tags, etc.) allow setting object-level permissions with optional `owner` and / or a `set_permissions` parameters... If these parameters are supplied the object's permissions will be overwritten, assuming the authenticated user has permission to do so (the user must be the object owner or a superuser).

findings.suggested_fix: Restore PassUserMixin in the SearchResultSerializer inheritance chain in src/documents/serialisers.py (line 799) to ensure user context is passed to the serializer, enabling object-level permission checks on documents returned in search results.

## Authorization

The REST api provides four different forms of authentication.

1.  Basic authentication

    Authorize by providing a HTTP header in the form

    ```
    Authorization: Basic <credentials>
    ```

    where `credentials` is a base64-encoded string of
    `<username>:<password>`

2.  Session authentication

    When you're logged into paperless in your browser, you're
    automatically logged into the API as well and don't need to provide
    any authorization headers.

3.  Token authentication

    You can create (or re-create) an API token by opening the "My Profile"
    link in the user dropdown found in the web UI and clicking the circular
    arrow button.

    Paperless also offers an endpoint to acquire authentication tokens.

    POST a username and password as a form or json string to
    `/api/token/` and paperless will respond with a token, if the login
    data is correct. This token can be used to authenticate other
    requests with the following HTTP header:

    ```
    Authorization: Token <token>
    ```

    Tokens can also be managed in the Django admin.

4.  Remote User authentication

    If enabled (see
    [configuration](configuration.md#PAPERLESS_ENABLE_HTTP_REMOTE_USER_API)),
    you can authenticate against the API using Remote User auth.

By default, the API will return a truncated version of object-level

granted). You can pass the parameter `full_perms=true` to API calls to view the
full permissions of objects in a format that mirrors the `set_permissions`
parameter above.

The API supports various bulk-editing operations which are executed asynchronously.

For bulk operations on documents, use the endpoint `/api/documents/bulk_edit/` which accepts
